nodes.name: TiO2 surface alkalization
nodes.procedure: 200 mg of ground TiO2 nanosheets was dispersed in 0.01M NaOH aqueous solution. After 3 h, the TiO2 was centrifuged and redispersed in deionized (DI) water through multiple cycles until the supernatant reached pH = 9, ensuring a negatively charged TiO2 surface for cation adsorption.

unit_operations.name: Washing cycles
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: centrifuged and redispersed in deionized (DI) water through multiple cycles until the supernatant reached pH = 9

nodes.name: Ni cation adsorption and drying
nodes.procedure: NiCl2 (Sigma-Aldrich) aqueous solution (containing Ni equivalent to 1 wt% of TiO2) was added to the alkalized TiO2 suspension and stirred for 12 h prior to centrifugation. Complete metal cation adsorption was confirmed by testing the first supernatant with NaBH4 (Thermo Fisher), which showed no color change. The cation-loaded TiO2 was washed with DI water and dried at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Ir anion phase-transfer adsorption
nodes.procedure: The dried cation-loaded TiO2 was subsequently used for complex metal anion adsorption IrCl6^3- (Na3IrCl6, Sigma-Aldrich) with controlled theoretical anion/cation atomic ratios. Anion solutions were prepared via a phase-transfer method using tetrabutylammonium cations (TBA+) in dichloromethane (TBA+/anion molar ratio = 3) under vortex mixing. After centrifugation, the dichloromethane phase was retained, and mixed with cation-loaded TiO2 in dichloromethane. After 12 h of stirring, TiO2-supported double complex salts were centrifuged, dried at room temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiIr0.5/TiO2 shows sub-2 nm bimetallic nanoclusters with intertwined Ni-Ir atomic distribution, average size up to 1.61 nm; monometallic Ni/TiO2 and Ir/TiO2 show sub-1.2 nm clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) analysis revealed that Ni species or Ir species on TiO2 exhibited sub-1.2 nm clusters... whereas the NiIrx nanoclusters on TiO2 showed an increase in size, progressively reaching up to 1.61 nm with higher Ir content.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS line scans and elemental mapping confirm intimate contact between Ni and Ir atoms in NiIr0.5/TiO2 nanoclusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS line scans (Fig.1g) and elemental mapping (Fig. 1h and Supplementary Fig. 5d-i) confirmed the intimate contact between Ni and Ir atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm exclusive anatase-phase TiO2 with no detectable metallic Ni or Ir reflections, consistent with sub-2 nm cluster dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns confirm exclusive anatase-phase TiO2 (Supplementary Fig. 6), with no detectable reflections from metallic Ni or Ir phases.

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Ir L3-edge and Ni K-edge XANES reveal partially oxidized states: Ir/TiO2 (+3.6), NiIr0.5/TiO2 Ir (+2.7), Ni/TiO2 Ni (+1.6), NiIr0.5/TiO2 Ni (+1.8), indicating Ni to Ir electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Normalized Ir L3-edge and Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) analysis reveal partially oxidized states of Ni and Ir... Linear combination fitting shows higher Ir oxidation in Ir/TiO2(+3.6) than NiIr0.5/TiO2(+2.7), and more reduced Ni in Ni/TiO2(+1.6) versus NiIr0.5/TiO2(+1.8).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge EXAFS shows Ir-O at ~1.60Å, Ir-Ir at ~2.56Å, and Ni-Ir scattering at 2.18Å in NiIrx/TiO2 samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) at the Ir L3-edge provides atomic-scale coordination details (Fig. 1i). All samples exhibit a prominent peak at ∼1.60Å and a relatively weaker peak at ∼2.56Å, corresponding to Ir-O scattering and Ir-Ir scattering, respectively. Notably, NiIrx/TiO2 samples exhibit an additional peak at 2.18 Å, which can be attributed to Ni-Ir scattering.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ CO-DRIFTS shows intense *CO chemisorption (2100-1990 cm⁻¹) on Ir-containing samples scaling with Ir content; NiIr_x/TiO2 shows Ir-(CO) peak shift 2063→2044 cm⁻¹ with increasing Ir due to Ni-to-Ir electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ CO probe molecule diffuse reflectance infrared fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) analyses... Ir-containing samples (NiIrx/TiO2, Ir/TiO2) display intense *CO chemisorption bands (2100-1990 cm⁻¹)... In NiIrx/TiO2, the dominant Ir-(CO) peak progressively shifts downward (2063→2044 cm⁻¹) with increasing Ir content.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES confirms controlled metal loadings across NiIr_x/TiO2 samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) confirms controlled metal loadings across NiIr_x/TiO2 samples (Supplementary Fig. 1 and Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES confirms controlled metal loadings across NiIr_x/TiO2 samples with sublinear increase in Ir/Ni ratios suggesting saturation of Ir adsorption onto pre-adsorbed Ni sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) confirms controlled metal loadings across NiIr_x/TiO2 samples (Supplementary Fig. 1 and Table S1), where x denotes the Ir/Ni theoretical atomic ratio. The sublinear increase in Ir/Ni ratios with x suggests saturation of Ir adsorption onto pre-adsorbed Ni sites.
